title: Making, Letting, and Getting Someone to Do Something
goal: Use common Bokmål causative patterns with an object plus infinitive or adjective.

objectives.statement: Use common Bokmål causative patterns with an object plus infinitive or adjective.

sections.title: A busy afternoon at the community centre

spans.value: Sara coordinates activities at a community centre. A photographer is coming to take pictures for the centre’s website, but the main room is still untidy. Sara asks her colleague Jonas for help.
Fotografen kommer om en time, og rommet ser fortsatt rotete ut.

blocks.translation: The photographer is coming in an hour, and the room still looks untidy.

spans.value: Jeg ba Emil rydde stolene, men han er ikke ferdig.

blocks.translation: I asked Emil to arrange the chairs, but he isn’t finished.

spans.value: Kan du få ham til å skynde seg?

blocks.translation: Can you get him to hurry?

spans.value: Ja. Skal jeg be Nora flytte bordene også?

blocks.translation: Yes. Should I ask Nora to move the tables too?

spans.value: Nei, la henne gjøre ferdig plakatene først.

blocks.translation: No, let her finish the posters first.

spans.value: Greit. Fotografen vil sikkert flytte på noen ting selv.

blocks.translation: All right. The photographer will probably want to move some things herself.

spans.value: Det går bra. La henne bestemme hvor stolene skal stå.

blocks.translation: That’s fine. Let her decide where the chairs should be.

spans.value: Du virker stresset.
Litt. Men det gjør meg roligere at du hjelper til.

blocks.translation: A little. But it makes me calmer that you’re helping.

spans.value: Da får jeg Emil til å rydde raskere, og så lager jeg kaffe.

blocks.translation: Then I’ll get Emil to tidy up faster, and then I’ll make coffee.

spans.value: The scene involves three different kinds of influence. Sara wants Jonas to cause Emil to act. She allows Nora to continue her work. Jonas’s help changes Sara’s emotional state. Bokmål uses different patterns for these meanings:

no.value: få noen til å gjøre noe
gjøre noen rolig, glad eller sint

en.value: make someone calm, happy, or angry

spans.value: The key choice is not simply how to translate the English verb make. You must first decide what kind of result you mean: causing an action, allowing an action, or causing a state.

sections.title: Getting someone to act: få noen til å + infinitive

spans.value: Use
få + object + til å + infinitive
when one person causes, persuades, encourages, or arranges for another person to do something.
Here the
object (objekt)
is the person who performs the action. The final verb appears in the
infinitive (infinitiv)

no.value: Sara får Emil til å rydde.

en.value: Sara gets Emil to tidy up.

spans.value: Sara causes or persuades Emil to do the tidying. Emil is the object of får, but he is also the person who performs rydde.
The pattern is:
person causing the action + få + person acting + til å + action
Compare the roles:

no.value: Sara får Jonas til å rydde rommet.

en.value: Sara gets Jonas to tidy the room.

spans.value: In the first sentence, Jonas acts independently. In the second, Sara causes or persuades him to act.
The verb få changes form normally according to tense:

no.value: Jeg får henne til å ringe kunden.

en.value: I get her to call the customer.

no.value: Jeg fikk henne til å ringe kunden.

en.value: I got her to call the customer.

no.value: Jeg skal få henne til å ringe kunden.

en.value: I will get her to call the customer.

spans.value: The person who performs the action may be a noun or an object pronoun:

no.value: Vi fikk naboen til å åpne døra.

en.value: We got the neighbour to open the door.

no.value: Vi fikk ham til å åpne døra.

en.value: We got him to open the door.

no.value: Læreren fikk oss til å lese teksten høyt.

en.value: The teacher got us to read the text aloud.

no.value: Barna fikk meg til å le.

spans.value: Common object pronouns include meg, deg, ham, henne, oss and dem.
What kind of pressure does få express?

Få noen til å gjøre noe tells us that someone’s influence produced an action. It does not, by itself, say exactly how. The person may ask, persuade, encourage, or arrange matters so that the action happens.

no.value: Hun fikk broren sin til å kjøre henne til stasjonen.

en.value: She got her brother to drive her to the station.

spans.value: This could mean that she asked him and he agreed. It does not necessarily imply force.

no.value: Sjefen fikk alle til å bli igjen etter møtet.

en.value: The manager got everyone to stay after the meeting.

spans.value: The situation may involve authority, but the grammar itself focuses on the result: everyone stayed because of the manager’s influence.
A common mistake: missing til
Do not place the second infinitive directly after the object with få.
Incorrect pattern:

en.value: She got me to call the customer.

spans.value: Standard Bokmål uses til å:

no.value: Hun fikk meg til å ringe kunden.

en.value: She got me to call the customer.

spans.value: Remember the complete link:
få noen til å gjøre noe

sections.title: Letting someone act: la noen + infinitive

spans.value: Use
la + object + infinitive
when someone permits an action or does not prevent it.

no.value: Sara lar Nora gjøre ferdig plakatene.

en.value: Sara lets Nora finish the posters.

spans.value: Nora performs the action. Sara allows it to happen.
The infinitive after the object appears
without å
, sometimes called the
bare infinitive (infinitiv uten å)

en.value: We let the children play outside.
They let me use the kitchen.

spans.value: The pattern is:
person allowing the action + la + person acting + infinitive without å
The present-tense form is lar, and the past-tense form is lot:

en.value: She lets me borrow the bicycle.
She let me borrow the bicycle.

spans.value: These constructions can describe the same two people and the same action, but they show different relationships.

no.value: Sara fikk Jonas til å flytte bordet.

en.value: Sara got Jonas to move the table.
Sara let Jonas move the table.

spans.value: In the first sentence, Sara’s influence causes Jonas to move it. Perhaps she asks him or persuades him.
In the second sentence, Jonas wants or intends to move it, and Sara permits him to do so.
Another contrast:

no.value: Moren fikk barnet til å spise suppa.

en.value: The mother got the child to eat the soup.
The mother let the child eat the soup.

spans.value: The first sentence suggests that the child needed encouragement or persuasion. The second focuses on permission.
A common mistake: adding å after la
English learners may expect an infinitive marker before every infinitive. After la + object, Bokmål does not use å.
Incorrect pattern:

no.value: ✗ De lot oss å vente inne.

spans.value: Correct pattern:
The contrast is worth learning as two complete frames:

sections.title: Causing a state: gjøre noen + adjective

spans.value: Sometimes the result is not an action performed by the object. Instead, something causes a person or thing to enter a state. Bokmål commonly uses
gjøre + object + adjective
An
adjective (adjektiv)
describes the resulting state.

no.value: Den høye musikken gjør meg sliten.

en.value: The loud music makes me tired.

spans.value: The pattern is:
cause + gjøre + affected person or thing + resulting adjective
Compare an ordinary description with a caused state:
The first sentence describes Sara’s state. The second introduces a cause.
The subject does not have to be a person:

en.value: The wait makes the children impatient.

no.value: Det varme lyset gjorde rommet hyggelig.

en.value: The warm light made the room pleasant.

spans.value: The adjective describes the object, not the subject. In the following sentence, trøtt describes meg:
It does not describe reisen.
Agreement in the resulting adjective
The adjective normally agrees with the person or thing whose resulting state it describes.

en.value: The message made the children nervous.
The paint made the room brighter.

spans.value: The central causative pattern remains gjøre + object + adjective. Familiar adjective agreement still applies inside that pattern.

sections.title: Do not copy English make mechanically

spans.value: English uses make before both actions and adjectives:
en: She made me call.
en: She made me nervous.
Bokmål normally separates these meanings:

no.value: Hun fikk meg til å ringe.

spans.value: Do not use gjøre + object + infinitive as a general translation of English make someone do something.
Incorrect pattern:
Use få + object + til å + infinitive for the caused action:

no.value: Hun fikk meg til å ringe.

spans.value: Use gjøre + object + adjective when the result is a state:
The object occupies a similar position in all three constructions, but what follows it tells us what kind of result is involved.
Meaning:
Cause or get someone to act.
Bokmål pattern:
få + object + til å + infinitive.
Example:

no.value: Jeg fikk ham til å vente.

spans.value: Meaning:
Permit someone to act.
Bokmål pattern:
la + object + bare infinitive.
Example:
Meaning:
Cause someone to be in a state.
Bokmål pattern:
gjøre + object + adjective.
Example:
Notice how ham has a different relationship to each final element:

no.value: Jeg fikk ham til å vente.

spans.value: He waits because of my influence.
He waits because I permit or do not prevent it.
He does not perform irritert as an action. Irritert describes his resulting state.
A useful decision sequence is:

items.value: Does the object perform an action because someone causes or arranges it? Use få noen til å gjøre noe.
Does the object perform an action because someone permits it? Use la noen gjøre noe.
Does the object enter a state described by an adjective? Use gjøre noen glad, rolig, sint, and similar expressions.

spans.value: An hour later, the photographer, Ingrid, arrives.
Her ser det fint ut! Hvordan ble dere ferdige så fort?

blocks.translation: It looks good here! How did you finish so quickly?

spans.value: Jonas fikk Emil til å rydde stolene, og jeg lot Nora gjøre ferdig plakatene.

blocks.translation: Jonas got Emil to arrange the chairs, and I let Nora finish the posters.

spans.value: Emil fikk faktisk meg til å flytte bordene en gang til.

blocks.translation: Emil actually got me to move the tables one more time.

spans.value: De sto bedre nær vinduet.

blocks.translation: They looked better near the window.

spans.value: Jeg er enig. Lyset gjør rommet mye hyggeligere.

blocks.translation: I agree. The light makes the room much more pleasant.

spans.value: Og kaffen gjorde alle litt mer våkne.

blocks.translation: And the coffee made everyone a little more alert.

spans.value: The roles have shifted. Emil was originally the person whom Jonas influenced, but later Emil gets Jonas to act. This shows why word order matters: the object after få identifies the person who performs the infinitive action.
Compare:

no.value: Jonas fikk Emil til å flytte bordet.

en.value: Jonas got Emil to move the table.

no.value: Emil fikk Jonas til å flytte bordet.

en.value: Emil got Jonas to move the table.

spans.value: The vocabulary is almost identical, but the people exchange roles.

sections.title: Cumulative transfer: preparing a family dinner

spans.value: Now transfer the same patterns to a new everyday situation. A family is preparing dinner for several guests. One person persuades a relative to buy bread, another permits the children to decorate the table, and an unexpected delay changes everyone’s mood.
Without looking back, recall the Bokmål frames for getting someone to act, letting someone act, and making someone or something enter a state.

prompt.value: In Sara and Jonas's community-centre dialogue, read these selected lines. Identify the meaning relationship in each line. Pronoun forms and word order are supporting context, not separate scoring goals. 1. Sara får Jonas til å rydde bordene. 2. Sara lar Jonas hvile litt. 3. Bråket gjør Jonas trøtt.

options.text: 1: tillater en handling; 2: forårsaker en handling; 3: forårsaker en tilstand.
options.why: The meanings of lines 1 and 2 are reversed.

options.text: 1: forårsaker en tilstand; 2: tillater en handling; 3: forårsaker en handling.
options.why: Lines 1 and 3 are assigned the wrong result type.

options.text: 1: forårsaker en handling; 2: tillater en handling; 3: forårsaker en tilstand.
options.why: Line 1 expresses causing an action, line 2 permission, and line 3 causing a state.

stem.value: Choose the complete meaning classification for lines 1–3.

prompt.value: At an everyday workplace, Sara influences Jonas to clean the meeting room. Construct the complete Bokmål sentence. Make Sara the subject, Jonas the object, and use få + object + til å + infinitive.

explanation.value: Use få plus the person affected plus til å plus infinitive when someone gets another person to perform an action.

prompt.value: Jonas wants to go home early, and Sara gives him permission. Choose the Bokmål sentence that expresses permission rather than causing Jonas to start the action.

options.text: Sara får Jonas til å gå hjem tidlig.
options.why: Få expresses causing Jonas to perform the action, not simply giving permission.

options.text: Sara lar Jonas gå hjem tidlig.
options.why: La expresses permission with the object followed by a bare infinitive.

stem.value: Which sentence matches the intended relationship?

prompt.value: At the community centre, loud music causes the neighbours to become angry. Build the complete Bokmål sentence with gjøre + object + adjective. Use the plural adjective form that describes naboene.

explanation.value: Use gjøre plus object plus adjective for a result: musikken gjør naboene sinte.

prompt.value: In two paired situations, Sara causes Jonas to wash the dishes, and a long journey makes Nora tired. Choose the Bokmål pair that preserves an action result in the first situation and a state result in the second. Permission with la is not scored.

options.text: Sara får Jonas til å vaske opp. Den lange reisen gjør Nora trøtt.
options.why: Få expresses the caused action, while gjøre expresses the caused state.

options.text: Sara lar Jonas vaske opp. Den lange reisen gjør Nora trøtt.
options.why: The first sentence expresses permission instead of causing the action.

options.text: Sara får Jonas til å vaske opp. Den lange reisen får Nora til å sove.
options.why: The second sentence uses an action construction instead of the required adjective state construction.

stem.value: Which pair uses the correct construction for each intended result?

prompt.value: At the community centre, Emil gives Jonas permission to open the door. Construct one complete Bokmål sentence. Put Emil as subject and Jonas as object, and use la + object + bare infinitive.

explanation.value: Use la plus person plus infinitive for permission: Emil lar Jonas åpne døren.

prompt.value: Write a short connected account in Norwegian about family members preparing dinner. Include one caused action using få + object + til å + infinitive, one permitted action using la + object + bare infinitive, and one caused emotional or physical state using gjøre + object + adjective. Each sentence should express one clear relationship and fit the family-dinner setting.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the Norwegian response against the task and report evidence for each criterion. Accept natural Bokmål variants when they preserve the required causative meaning and construction.

criteria.instruction: Includes one natural Bokmål sentence in which one family member causes another to perform an action with få + object + til å + infinitive.
Includes one natural Bokmål sentence in which one family member gives another permission with la + object + bare infinitive.
Includes one natural Bokmål sentence using gjøre + object + adjective to express a caused emotional or physical state.
Each required sentence expresses one clear relationship, and the account remains coherent in the family-dinner setting.
